tagline: Twenty-four miles of dirt across the breaks.
intro: From the Escondida exit on I-25 the byway runs about 24 miles on unpaved county road, out to the east and then down to US 380. It climbs onto bench land above the floodplain and crosses arroyos draining to the river, through the quebradas, the breaks, that give the country its name.

The Sevilleta refuge lies a few miles north and Bosque del Apache a few miles south. In between there are badlands, box canyons and multicolored cliffs, and no restrooms or drinking water anywhere along the road.

moments.title: Minas del Chupadero
moments.text: An abandoned mining ground along the byway, with a shaft, an adit and several exploration pits.

moments.title: The banded ridges
moments.text: About midway the banding shows in the north-south ridges, red and yellow sandstone, red and purple shale and white to gray limestone.

practical: A high-clearance vehicle is recommended. The road has blind curves and steep hills, can become difficult or impossible to drive after heavy rain, and has no water or restrooms; the nearest food and fuel are in Socorro.
